paper_id: Lu et al. - 2007 - Dynamic Key-Updating Privacy-Preserving Authentication for RFID Systems
title: Dynamic Key-Updating: Privacy-Preserving Authentication for RFID Systems
motivation: RFID tags auto-emit serial numbers enabling silent tracking; existing tree-based protocols lack key-updating making them vulnerable to compromising attacks
problem_framing: How to enable dynamic key-updating in tree-based RFID auth while maintaining consistency across shared keys without mass tag updates
key_insight: Temporary keys and state bits allow each non-leaf node to auto-update only after all children update—cascading updates without coordination overhead
method_signature: Tree-walking ID with per-node temporary-key + state-bit tracking for lazy cascading key renewal
evaluation_criteria: Correlated-exposing probability under compromising attack; key-updating latency; O(log N) identification complexity
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Static tree approaches cannot solve key-updating; updating root-adjacent keys influences half of all tags making the problem intractable without SPA
evidence_for_taste: static tree architecture is not capable
consistent and dynamic key-updating mechanisms have scarcely been seen
major challenge of dynamic key-updating is consistency
enlarging δ does not help much
such a solution is not practical
thinking_moves: 把全局一致性协调难题转换为局部状态传播问题
引入临时存储使旧密钥在过渡期内仍可被其他标签使用
通过状态位追踪子节点更新进度实现自动级联
从妥协攻击后果反推需要前向保密和动态密钥更新
extraction_notes: Authors identify existing tree protocols as vulnerable due to static key storage; SPA solves by lazy updating with temp keys and state bits; performance validated via prototype on 40 RF Code tags with SHA-1 hash
